# Shichikuji and Power Grid

Shichikuji is the new resident deity of the South Black Snail Temple. Her first job is as follows:



There are $n$ new cities located in Prefecture X. Cities are numbered from $1$ to $n$. City $i$ is located $x_i$ km North of the shrine and $y_i$ km East of the shrine. It is possible that $(x_i, y_i) = (x_j, y_j)$ even when $i \ne j$.



Shichikuji must provide electricity to each city either by building a power station in that city, or by making a connection between that city and another one that already has electricity. So the City has electricity if it has a power station in it or it is connected to a City which has electricity by a direct connection or via a chain of connections.



- Building a power station in City $i$ will cost $c_i$ yen;

- Making a connection between City $i$ and City $j$ will cost $k_i + k_j$ yen **per km of wire** used for the connection. However, wires can only go the cardinal directions (North, South, East, West). Wires can cross each other. Each wire must have both of its endpoints in some cities. If City $i$ and City $j$ are connected by a wire, the wire will go through any shortest path from City $i$ to City $j$. Thus, the length of the wire if City $i$ and City $j$ are connected is $|x_i - x_j| + |y_i - y_j|$ km.



Shichikuji wants to do this job spending as little money as possible, since according to her, there isn't really anything else in the world other than money. However, she died when she was only in fifth grade so she is not smart enough for this. And thus, the new resident deity asks for your help.



And so, you have to provide Shichikuji with the following information: minimum amount of yen needed to provide electricity to all cities, the cities in which power stations will be built, and the connections to be made.



If there are multiple ways to choose the cities and the connections to obtain the construction of minimum price, then print any of them.



## Input



First line of input contains a single integer $n$ ($1 \leq n \leq 2000$) — the number of cities.



Then, $n$ lines follow. The $i$-th line contains two space-separated integers $x_i$ ($1 \leq x_i \leq 10^6$) and $y_i$ ($1 \leq y_i \leq 10^6$) — the coordinates of the $i$-th city.



The next line contains $n$ space-separated integers $c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$ ($1 \leq c_i \leq 10^9$) — the cost of building a power station in the $i$-th city.



The last line contains $n$ space-separated integers $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_n$ ($1 \leq k_i \leq 10^9$).



## Output



In the first line print a single integer, denoting the minimum amount of yen needed.



Then, print an integer $v$ — the number of power stations to be built.



Next, print $v$ space-separated integers, denoting the indices of cities in which a power station will be built. Each number should be from $1$ to $n$ and all numbers should be pairwise distinct. You can print the numbers in arbitrary order.



After that, print an integer $e$ — the number of connections to be made.



Finally, print $e$ pairs of integers $a$ and $b$ ($1 \le a, b \le n$, $a \ne b$), denoting that a connection between City $a$ and City $b$ will be made. Each unordered pair of cities should be included at most once (for each $(a, b)$ there should be no more $(a, b)$ or $(b, a)$ pairs). You can print the pairs in arbitrary order.



If there are multiple ways to choose the cities and the connections to obtain the construction of minimum price, then print any of them.



## Note



For the answers given in the samples, refer to the following diagrams (cities with power stations are colored green, other cities are colored blue, and wires are colored red):



![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/90852f0207479bf2b34b5ab73f94befafb8be3d3.png)



For the first example, the cost of building power stations in all cities is $3 + 2 + 3 = 8$. It can be shown that no configuration costs less than 8 yen.



For the second example, the cost of building a power station in City 2 is 2. The cost of connecting City 1 and City 2 is $2 \cdot (3 + 2) = 10$. The cost of connecting City 2 and City 3 is $3 \cdot (2 + 3) = 15$. Thus the total cost is $2 + 10 + 15 = 27$. It can be shown that no configuration costs less than 27 yen.

# Shichikuji 与电网

Shichikuji 是南黑蜗牛神庙的新任驻守神明。她的第一项工作如下：



在 X 县有 $n$ 座新城市。城市编号从 $1$ 到 $n$。城市 $i$ 位于神庙以北 $x_i$ 千米、以东 $y_i$ 千米处。即使 $i \ne j$，也可能出现 $(x_i, y_i) = (x_j, y_j)$。



Shichikuji 必须为每座城市供电，方式要么是在该城市建造一座发电站，要么是将该城市与另一座已经通电的城市连接起来。因此，如果城市中有一座发电站，或者它通过直接连接或一连串连接与一座有电的城市相连，那么该城市就有电。



- 在城市 $i$ 建造一座发电站将花费 $c_i$ 日元；

- 在城市 $i$ 和城市 $j$ 之间建立连接将花费 $k_i + k_j$ 日元**每千米电线**。然而，电线只能沿基本方向（北、南、东、西）铺设。电线可以相互交叉。每根电线的两个端点都必须位于某些城市中。如果城市 $i$ 和城市 $j$ 通过一根电线连接，则该电线将沿着从城市 $i$ 到城市 $j$ 的任意最短路径铺设。因此，如果城市 $i$ 和城市 $j$ 相连，则电线的长度为 $|x_i - x_j| + |y_i - y_j|$ 千米。



Shichikuji 想尽可能少花钱完成这项工作，因为在她看来，世界上除了钱真的没有别的东西了。然而，她年仅五年级就去世了，所以她不够聪明，无法完成这件事。因此，这位新任驻守神明请求你的帮助。



因此，你必须向 Shichikuji 提供以下信息：为所有城市供电所需的最少日元金额、将建造发电站的城市，以及要建立的连接。



如果有多种选择城市和连接的方式可以获得最低价格的建造方案，则输出其中任意一种。



## 输入



输入的第一行包含一个整数 $n$（$1 \leq n \leq 2000$）—— 城市数量。



接下来有 $n$ 行。第 $i$ 行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 $x_i$（$1 \leq x_i \leq 10^6$）和 $y_i$（$1 \leq y_i \leq 10^6$）—— 第 $i$ 座城市的坐标。



下一行包含 $n$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$（$1 \leq c_i \leq 10^9$）—— 在第 $i$ 座城市建造发电站的费用。



最后一行包含 $n$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_n$（$1 \leq k_i \leq 10^9$）。



## 输出



在第一行输出一个整数，表示所需的最少日元金额。



然后，输出一个整数 $v$——要建造的发电站数量。



接下来，输出 $v$ 个以空格分隔的整数，表示将建造发电站的城市编号。每个数字应在 $1$ 到 $n$ 之间，且所有数字应两两不同。你可以按任意顺序输出这些数字。



之后，输出一个整数 $e$——要建立的连接数量。



最后，输出 $e$ 对整数 $a$ 和 $b$（$1 \le a, b \le n$，$a \ne b$），表示将在城市 $a$ 和城市 $b$ 之间建立连接。每对无序城市最多应包含一次（对于每个 $(a, b)$，不应有超过一个 $(a, b)$ 或 $(b, a)$ 对）。你可以按任意顺序输出这些对。



如果有多种选择城市和连接的方式可以获得最低价格的建造方案，则输出其中任意一种。



## 提示



对于样例中给出的答案，请参考以下图示（有发电站的城市为绿色，其他城市为蓝色，电线为红色）：



![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/90852f0207479bf2b34b5ab73f94befafb8be3d3.png)



对于第一个样例，在所有城市建造发电站的费用为 $3 + 2 + 3 = 8$。可以证明没有配置的费用低于 8 日元。



对于第二个样例，在城市 2 建造发电站的费用为 2。连接城市 1 和城市 2 的费用为 $2 \cdot (3 + 2) = 10$。连接城市 2 和城市 3 的费用为 $3 \cdot (2 + 3) = 15$。因此总费用为 $2 + 10 + 15 = 27$。可以证明没有配置的费用低于 27 日元。

# Paths in a Complete Binary Tree

*T* is a complete binary tree consisting of *n* vertices. It means that exactly one vertex is a root, and each vertex is either a leaf (and doesn't have children) or an inner node (and has exactly two children). All leaves of a complete binary tree have the same depth (distance from the root). So *n* is a number such that *n* + 1 is a power of 2.

In the picture you can see a complete binary tree with *n* = 15.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7cf45e9d9e44d8d0a3972224b62a35dd86b5f1b3.png)

Vertices are numbered from 1 to *n* in a special recursive way: we recursively assign numbers to all vertices from the left subtree (if current vertex is not a leaf), then assign a number to the current vertex, and then recursively assign numbers to all vertices from the right subtree (if it exists). In the picture vertices are numbered exactly using this algorithm. It is clear that for each size of a complete binary tree exists exactly one way to give numbers to all vertices. This way of numbering is called symmetric.

You have to write a program that for given *n* answers *q* queries to the tree.

Each query consists of an integer number *u*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *u*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*) and a string *s*$_{i}$, where *u*$_{i}$ is the number of vertex, and *s*$_{i}$ represents the path starting from this vertex. String *s*$_{i}$ doesn't contain any characters other than '`L`', '`R`' and '`U`', which mean traverse to the left child, to the right child and to the parent, respectively. Characters from *s*$_{i}$ have to be processed from left to right, considering that *u*$_{i}$ is the vertex where the path starts. If it's impossible to process a character (for example, to go to the left child of a leaf), then you have to skip it. The answer is the number of vertex where the path represented by *s*$_{i}$ ends.

For example, if *u*$_{i}$ = 4 and *s*$_{i}$ = «`UURL`», then the answer is 10.

## Input

The first line contains two integer numbers *n* and *q* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10$^{18}$, *q* ≥ 1). *n* is such that *n* + 1 is a power of 2.

The next 2*q* lines represent queries; each query consists of two consecutive lines. The first of these two lines contains *u*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *u*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*), the second contains non-empty string *s*$_{i}$. *s*$_{i}$ doesn't contain any characters other than '`L`', '`R`' and '`U`'.

It is guaranteed that the sum of lengths of *s*$_{i}$ (for each *i* such that 1 ≤ *i* ≤ *q*) doesn't exceed 10$^{5}$.

## Output

Print *q* numbers, *i*-th number must be the answer to the *i*-th query.
content.title: Paths in a Complete Binary Tree

# ## 完全二叉树中的路径



*T* 是一棵由 *n* 个顶点组成的完全二叉树。这意味着恰好有一个顶点是根，并且每个顶点要么是叶子（没有孩子），要么是内部节点（恰好有两个孩子）。完全二叉树的所有叶子都具有相同的深度（到根的距离）。因此 *n* 是一个使得 *n* + 1 是 2 的幂的数。



在图中你可以看到一棵 *n* = 15 的完全二叉树。



![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7cf45e9d9e44d8d0a3972224b62a35dd86b5f1b3.png)

顶点以特殊的递归方式从 1 到 *n* 编号：我们递归地为左子树中的所有顶点分配编号（如果当前顶点不是叶子），然后为当前顶点分配一个编号，然后递归地为右子树中的所有顶点分配编号（如果存在）。在图中，顶点正是使用此算法编号的。很明显，对于完全二叉树的每种大小，都存在恰好一种为所有顶点编号的方式。这种编号方式称为对称的。



你必须编写一个程序，对于给定的 *n* 回答对树的 *q* 个查询。



每个查询由一个整数 *u*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *u*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*）和一个字符串 *s*$_{i}$ 组成，其中 *u*$_{i}$ 是顶点编号，*s*$_{i}$ 表示从该顶点开始的路径。字符串 *s*$_{i}$ 不包含除 '`L`'、'`R`' 和 '`U`' 之外的任何字符，它们分别表示遍历到左孩子、右孩子和父节点。*s*$_{i}$ 中的字符必须从左到右处理，考虑到 *u*$_{i}$ 是路径开始的顶点。如果无法处理某个字符（例如，走到叶子的左孩子），则必须跳过它。答案是 *s*$_{i}$ 所表示的路径结束的顶点编号。



例如，如果 *u*$_{i}$ = 4 且 *s*$_{i}$ = «`UURL`»，则答案是 10。



## 输入

第一行包含两个整数 *n* 和 *q*（1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10$^{18}$，*q* ≥ 1）。*n* 满足 *n* + 1 是 2 的幂。



接下来的 2*q* 行表示查询；每个查询由连续的两行组成。这两行中的第一行包含 *u*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *u*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*），第二行包含非空字符串 *s*$_{i}$。*s*$_{i}$ 不包含除 '`L`'、'`R`' 和 '`U`' 之外的任何字符。

保证所有 *s*$_{i}$ 的长度之和（对于每个满足 1 ≤ *i* ≤ *q* 的 *i*）不超过 10$^{5}$。

## 输出

输出 *q* 个数，第 *i* 个数必须是第 *i* 个询问的答案。

# Mages and Monsters

Vova plays a computer game known as Mages and Monsters. Vova's character is a mage. Though as he has just started, his character knows no spells.

Vova's character can learn new spells during the game. Every spell is characterized by two values *x*$_{i}$ and *y*$_{i}$ — damage per second and mana cost per second, respectively. Vova doesn't have to use a spell for an integer amount of seconds. More formally, if he uses a spell with damage *x* and mana cost *y* for *z* seconds, then he will deal *x*·*z* damage and spend *y*·*z* mana (no rounding). If there is no mana left (mana amount is set in the start of the game and it remains the same at the beginning of every fight), then character won't be able to use any spells. It is prohibited to use multiple spells simultaneously.

Also Vova can fight monsters. Every monster is characterized by two values *t*$_{j}$ and *h*$_{j}$ — monster kills Vova's character in *t*$_{j}$ seconds and has *h*$_{j}$ health points. Mana refills after every fight (or Vova's character revives with full mana reserve), so previous fights have no influence on further ones.

Vova's character kills a monster, if he deals *h*$_{j}$ damage to it in no more than *t*$_{j}$ seconds using his spells (it is allowed to use more than one spell in a fight) and spending no more mana than he had at the beginning of the fight. If monster's health becomes zero exactly in *t*$_{j}$ seconds (it means that the monster and Vova's character kill each other at the same time), then Vova wins the fight.

You have to write a program which can answer two types of queries:

- 1 *x* *y* — Vova's character learns new spell which deals *x* damage per second and costs *y* mana per second.

- 2 *t* *h* — Vova fights the monster which kills his character in *t* seconds and has *h* health points.

Note that queries are given in a different form. Also remember that Vova's character knows no spells at the beginning of the game.

For every query of second type you have to determine if Vova is able to win the fight with corresponding monster.

## Input

The first line contains two integer numbers *q* and *m* (2 ≤ *q* ≤ 10$^{5}$, 1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10$^{12}$) — the number of queries and the amount of mana at the beginning of every fight.

*i*-th of each next *q* lines contains three numbers *k*$_{i}$, *a*$_{i}$ and *b*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *k*$_{i}$ ≤ 2, 1 ≤ *a*$_{i}$, *b*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{6}$).

Using them you can restore queries this way: let *j* be the index of the last query of second type with positive answer (*j* = 0 if there were none of these).

- If *k*$_{i}$ = 1, then character learns spell with *x* = (*a*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1, *y* = (*b*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1.

- If *k*$_{i}$ = 2, then you have to determine if Vova is able to win the fight against monster with *t* = (*a*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1, *h* = (*b*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1.

## Output

For every query of second type print `YES` if Vova is able to win the fight with corresponding monster and `NO` otherwise.

## Note

In first example Vova's character at first learns the spell with 5 damage and 10 mana cost per second. Next query is a fight with monster which can kill character in 20 seconds and has 50 health points. Vova kills it in 10 seconds (spending 100 mana). Next monster has 52 health, so Vova can't deal that much damage with only 100 mana.

# Mages and Monsters

Vova 正在玩一款名为 Mages and Monsters 的电脑游戏。Vova 的角色是一名法师。不过由于他刚刚开始，他的角色不会任何法术。

Vova 的角色可以在游戏过程中学习新法术。每个法术由两个值刻画：*x*$_{i}$ 和 *y*$_{i}$——分别为每秒伤害和每秒法力消耗。Vova 不必以整数秒来使用法术。更形式化地说，如果他使用一个伤害为 *x*、法力消耗为 *y* 的法术持续 *z* 秒，那么他将造成 *x*·*z* 点伤害并消耗 *y*·*z* 点法力（不取整）。如果没有剩余法力（法力值在游戏开始时设定，并且在每场战斗开始时保持不变），那么角色将无法使用任何法术。禁止同时使用多个法术。

此外，Vova 还可以与怪物战斗。每个怪物由两个值刻画：*t*$_{j}$ 和 *h*$_{j}$——怪物会在 *t*$_{j}$ 秒内杀死 Vova 的角色，并且拥有 *h*$_{j}$ 点生命值。每场战斗后法力会恢复（或者说 Vova 的角色会以满法力复活），因此之前的战斗不会影响之后的战斗。

如果 Vova 的角色在不超过 *t*$_{j}$ 秒内使用他的法术对怪物造成 *h*$_{j}$ 点伤害（一场战斗中允许使用不止一个法术），并且消耗的法力不超过战斗开始时拥有的法力，那么他就杀死了怪物。如果怪物的生命值恰好在 *t*$_{j}$ 秒时变为零（这意味着怪物和 Vova 的角色同时杀死对方），那么 Vova 赢得这场战斗。

你需要编写一个程序，能够回答两种类型的查询：

- 1 *x* *y*——Vova 的角色学习一个新法术，该法术每秒造成 *x* 点伤害并每秒消耗 *y* 点法力。

- 2 *t* *h*——Vova 与一个会在 *t* 秒内杀死他的角色并拥有 *h* 点生命值的怪物战斗。

注意，查询以不同的形式给出。还要记住，Vova 的角色在游戏开始时不会任何法术。

对于每个第二种类型的查询，你必须确定 Vova 是否能够赢得与对应怪物的战斗。

## 输入

第一行包含两个整数 *q* 和 *m*（2 ≤ *q* ≤ 10$^{5}$，1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10$^{12}$）——查询的数量以及每场战斗开始时的法力值。

接下来的 *q* 行中第 *i* 行包含三个数 *k*$_{i}$、*a*$_{i}$ 和 *b*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *k*$_{i}$ ≤ 2，1 ≤ *a*$_{i}$，*b*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{6}$）。

使用它们，你可以按如下方式还原查询：设 *j* 为第二条类型中答案为肯定的最后一个查询的编号（如果不存在这样的查询，则 *j* = 0）。

- 如果 *k*$_{i}$ = 1，则角色学会法术，其 *x* = (*a*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1，*y* = (*b*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1。

- 如果 *k*$_{i}$ = 2，则你需要判断 Vova 能否战胜具有 *t* = (*a*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1、*h* = (*b*$_{i}$ + *j*) *mod* 10$^{6}$ + 1 的怪物。

## 输出

对于每个第二条类型的查询，如果 Vova 能战胜对应的怪物，则输出 `YES`，否则输出 `NO`。

## 提示

在第一个样例中，Vova 的角色首先学会了每秒造成 5 点伤害、消耗 10 点法力的法术。下一个查询是与一个能在 20 秒内杀死角色且拥有 50 点生命值的怪物战斗。Vova 在 10 秒内杀死它（消耗 100 点法力）。下一个怪物有 52 点生命值，所以 Vova 仅用 100 点法力无法造成那么多伤害。

# The Contest

Pasha is participating in a contest on one well-known website. This time he wants to win the contest and will do anything to get to the first place!

This contest consists of *n* problems, and Pasha solves *i*th problem in *a*$_{i}$ time units (his solutions are always correct). At any moment of time he can be thinking about a solution to only one of the problems (that is, he cannot be solving two problems at the same time). The time Pasha spends to send his solutions is negligible. Pasha can send any number of solutions at the same moment.

Unfortunately, there are too many participants, and the website is not always working. Pasha received the information that the website will be working only during *m* time periods, *j*th period is represented by its starting moment *l*$_{j}$ and ending moment *r*$_{j}$. Of course, Pasha can send his solution only when the website is working. In other words, Pasha can send his solution at some moment *T* iff there exists a period *x* such that *l*$_{x}$ ≤ *T* ≤ *r*$_{x}$.

Pasha wants to know his best possible result. We need to tell him the minimal moment of time by which he is able to have solutions to all problems submitted, if he acts optimally, or say that it's impossible no matter how Pasha solves the problems.

## Input

The first line contains one integer *n* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000) — the number of problems. The second line contains *n* integers *a*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *a*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{5}$) — the time Pasha needs to solve *i*th problem.

The third line contains one integer *m* (0 ≤ *m* ≤ 1000) — the number of periods of time when the website is working. Next *m* lines represent these periods. *j*th line contains two numbers *l*$_{j}$ and *r*$_{j}$ (1 ≤ *l*$_{j}$ < *r*$_{j}$ ≤ 10$^{5}$) — the starting and the ending moment of *j*th period.

It is guaranteed that the periods are not intersecting and are given in chronological order, so for every *j* > 1 the condition *l*$_{j}$ > *r*$_{j - 1}$ is met.

## Output

If Pasha can solve and submit all the problems before the end of the contest, print the minimal moment of time by which he can have all the solutions submitted.

Otherwise print "-1" (without brackets).

## Note

In the first example Pasha can act like this: he solves the second problem in 4 units of time and sends it immediately. Then he spends 3 time units to solve the first problem and sends it 7 time units after the contest starts, because at this moment the website starts working again.

In the second example Pasha invents the solution only after the website stops working for the last time.

In the third example Pasha sends the solution exactly at the end of the first period.

# 比赛

帕夏正在参加一个知名网站上的比赛。这一次他想赢得比赛，并且会不惜一切代价登上第一名！

这场比赛由 *n* 道题组成，Pasha 解决第 *i* 道题需要 *a*$_{i}$ 个时间单位（他的解法总是正确的）。在任何时刻，他只能思考其中一道题的解法（也就是说，他不能同时解决两道题）。Pasha 发送他的解法所花费的时间可以忽略不计。Pasha 可以在同一时刻发送任意数量的解法。

不幸的是，参赛者太多了，而网站并不总是正常工作。Pasha 得知网站只会在 *m* 个时间段内工作，第 *j* 个时间段由其开始时刻 *l*$_{j}$ 和结束时刻 *r*$_{j}$ 表示。当然，Pasha 只能在网站工作时提交他的解答。换句话说，Pasha 可以在某个时刻 *T* 提交他的解答，当且仅当存在一个时间段 *x* 使得 *l*$_{x}$ ≤ *T* ≤ *r*$_{x}$。

帕夏想知道他可能取得的最好结果。我们需要告诉他，如果他采取最优策略，他能够提交所有问题的解答的最小时刻；或者说，无论帕夏如何解题，这都是不可能的。

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数 *n*（1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000）——题目的数量。第二行包含 *n* 个整数 *a*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *a*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{5}$）——Pasha 解决第 *i* 道题所需的时间。

第三行包含一个整数 *m*（0 ≤ *m* ≤ 1000）——网站工作的时间段数。接下来 *m* 行表示这些时间段。第 *j* 行包含两个数 *l*$_{j}$ 和 *r*$_{j}$（1 ≤ *l*$_{j}$ < *r*$_{j}$ ≤ 10$^{5}$）——第 *j* 个时间段的开始和结束时刻。

保证这些时间段互不相交，并且按时间顺序给出，因此对于每个 *j* > 1，都满足条件 *l*$_{j}$ > *r*$_{j - 1}$。

## ## 题目描述

给定一个长度为 \(2n\) 的数组 \(a\)，其中 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

我们称一个数对 \((i, j)\)（\(1 \le i < j \le 2n\)）是“好的”，当且仅当 \(a_i = a_j\)，并且区间 \([i, j]\) 中不存在两个相同的数。

请求出“好的”数对的数量。

## 输入格式

第一行一个整数 \(n\)（\(1 \le n \le 5 \times 10^5\)）。

第二行 \(2n\) 个整数 \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2n}\)（\(1 \le a_i \le n\)），保证 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，表示“好的”数对的数量。

## 样例输入 1

```
3
1 2 1 3 2 3
```

## 样例输出 1

```
2
```

## 样例解释 1

“好的”数对为 \((1, 3)\) 和 \((2, 5)\)。

## 样例输入 2

```
2
1 2 2 1
```

## 样例输出 2

```
0
```

## 样例解释 2

不存在“好的”数对。

## 约束

- \(1 \le n \le 5 \times 10^5\)
- \(1 \le a_i \le n\)
- \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

如果Pasha能在比赛结束前解决并提交所有题目，输出他能提交所有题解的最小时刻。

否则输出 "-1"（不含括号）。

## 注意

在第一个例子中，Pasha 可以这样行动：他用 4 单位时间解决第二个问题，并立即发送它。然后他花费 3 个时间单位解决第一道题，并在比赛开始后 7 个时间单位时提交它，因为此时网站重新开始工作。

在第二个例子中，Pasha 直到网站最后一次停止工作之后才想出解法。

在第三个例子中，Pasha 恰好在第一个时间段结束时提交解法。

# The Tag Game

Alice got tired of playing the tag game by the usual rules so she offered Bob a little modification to it. Now the game should be played on an undirected rooted tree of *n* vertices. Vertex `1` is the root of the tree.

Alice starts at vertex `1` and Bob starts at vertex *x* (*x* ≠ 1). The moves are made in turns, Bob goes first. In one move one can either stay at the current vertex or travel to the neighbouring one.

The game ends when Alice goes to the same vertex where Bob is standing. Alice wants to minimize the total number of moves and Bob wants to maximize it.

You should write a program which will determine how many moves will the game last.

## Input

The first line contains two integer numbers *n* and *x* (2 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$, 2 ≤ *x* ≤ *n*).

Each of the next *n* - 1 lines contains two integer numbers *a* and *b* (1 ≤ *a*, *b* ≤ *n*) — edges of the tree. It is guaranteed that the edges form a valid tree.

## Output

Print the total number of moves Alice and Bob will make.

## Note

In the first example the tree looks like this:

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/19db10c60e984271fd50b19d153bf0538f762ec3.png)

The red vertex is Alice's starting position, the blue one is Bob's. Bob will make the game run the longest by standing at the vertex `3` during all the game. So here are the moves:

B: stay at vertex `3`

A: go to vertex `2`

B: stay at vertex `3`

A: go to vertex `3`

In the second example the tree looks like this:

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ca6d5723922ddcb95fced46f31945771a79c2955.png)

The moves in the optimal strategy are:

B: go to vertex `3`

A: go to vertex `2`

B: go to vertex `4`

A: go to vertex `3`

B: stay at vertex `4`

A: go to vertex `4`

# Choosing The Commander

As you might remember from the previous round, Vova is currently playing a strategic game known as Rage of Empires.

Vova managed to build a large army, but forgot about the main person in the army - the commander. So he tries to hire a commander, and he wants to choose the person who will be respected by warriors.

Each warrior is represented by his personality — an integer number *p*$_{i}$. Each commander has two characteristics — his personality *p*$_{j}$ and leadership *l*$_{j}$ (both are integer numbers). Warrior *i* respects commander *j* only if ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8125d4c911c845cc506dda0bacc8675f2cf9f121.png) (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) is the bitwise excluding OR of *x* and *y*).

Initially Vova's army is empty. There are three different types of events that can happen with the army:

- 1 *p*$_{i}$ — one warrior with personality *p*$_{i}$ joins Vova's army;

- 2 *p*$_{i}$ — one warrior with personality *p*$_{i}$ leaves Vova's army;

- 3 *p*$_{i}$ *l*$_{i}$ — Vova tries to hire a commander with personality *p*$_{i}$ and leadership *l*$_{i}$.

For each event of the third type Vova wants to know how many warriors (counting only those who joined the army and haven't left yet) respect the commander he tries to hire.

## Input

The first line contains one integer *q* (1 ≤ *q* ≤ 100000) — the number of events.

Then *q* lines follow. Each line describes the event:

- 1 *p*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *p*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{8}$) — one warrior with personality *p*$_{i}$ joins Vova's army;

- 2 *p*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *p*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{8}$) — one warrior with personality *p*$_{i}$ leaves Vova's army (it is guaranteed that there is at least one such warrior in Vova's army by this moment);

- 3 *p*$_{i}$ *l*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *p*$_{i}$, *l*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{8}$) — Vova tries to hire a commander with personality *p*$_{i}$ and leadership *l*$_{i}$. There is at least one event of this type.

## Output

For each event of the third type print one integer — the number of warriors who respect the commander Vova tries to hire in the event.

## Note

In the example the army consists of two warriors with personalities 3 and 4 after first two events. Then Vova tries to hire a commander with personality 6 and leadership 3, and only one warrior respects him (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3d8e4cd0a5c3c0cdc8b35097f3dc7317604240a6.png), and 2 < 3, but ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4e3eeab99fa495ecdcd103c68de47dd72943016f.png), and 5 ≥ 3). Then warrior with personality 4 leaves, and when Vova tries to hire that commander again, there are no warriors who respect him.

# Sofa Thief

Yet another round on DecoForces is coming! Grandpa Maks wanted to participate in it but someone has stolen his precious sofa! And how can one perform well with such a major loss?

Fortunately, the thief had left a note for Grandpa Maks. This note got Maks to the sofa storehouse. Still he had no idea which sofa belongs to him as they all looked the same!

The storehouse is represented as matrix *n* × *m*. Every sofa takes two neighbouring by some side cells. No cell is covered by more than one sofa. There can be empty cells.

Sofa *A* is standing to the left of sofa *B* if there exist two such cells *a* and *b* that *x*$_{a}$ < *x*$_{b}$, *a* is covered by *A* and *b* is covered by *B*. Sofa *A* is standing to the top of sofa *B* if there exist two such cells *a* and *b* that *y*$_{a}$ < *y*$_{b}$, *a* is covered by *A* and *b* is covered by *B*. Right and bottom conditions are declared the same way.

Note that in all conditions *A* ≠ *B*. Also some sofa *A* can be both to the top of another sofa *B* and to the bottom of it. The same is for left and right conditions.

The note also stated that there are *cnt*$_{l}$ sofas to the left of Grandpa Maks's sofa, *cnt*$_{r}$ — to the right, *cnt*$_{t}$ — to the top and *cnt*$_{b}$ — to the bottom.

Grandpa Maks asks you to help him to identify his sofa. It is guaranteed that there is no more than one sofa of given conditions.

Output the number of Grandpa Maks's sofa. If there is no such sofa that all the conditions are met for it then output `-1`.

## Input

The first line contains one integer number *d* (1 ≤ *d* ≤ 10$^{5}$) — the number of sofas in the storehouse.

The second line contains two integer numbers *n*, *m* (1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10$^{5}$) — the size of the storehouse.

Next *d* lines contains four integer numbers *x*$_{1}$, *y*$_{1}$, *x*$_{2}$, *y*$_{2}$ (1 ≤ *x*$_{1}$, *x*$_{2}$ ≤ *n*, 1 ≤ *y*$_{1}$, *y*$_{2}$ ≤ *m*) — coordinates of the *i*-th sofa. It is guaranteed that cells (*x*$_{1}$, *y*$_{1}$) and (*x*$_{2}$, *y*$_{2}$) have common side, (*x*$_{1}$, *y*$_{1}$)  ≠  (*x*$_{2}$, *y*$_{2}$) and no cell is covered by more than one sofa.

The last line contains four integer numbers *cnt*$_{l}$, *cnt*$_{r}$, *cnt*$_{t}$, *cnt*$_{b}$ (0 ≤ *cnt*$_{l}$, *cnt*$_{r}$, *cnt*$_{t}$, *cnt*$_{b}$ ≤ *d* - 1).

## Output

Print the number of the sofa for which all the conditions are met. Sofas are numbered 1 through *d* as given in input. If there is no such sofa then print `-1`.

## Note

Let's consider the second example.

- The first sofa has 0 to its left, 2 sofas to its right ((1, 1) is to the left of both (5, 5) and (5, 4)), 0 to its top and 2 to its bottom (both 2nd and 3rd sofas are below).

- The second sofa has *cnt*$_{l}$ = 2, *cnt*$_{r}$ = 1, *cnt*$_{t}$ = 2 and *cnt*$_{b}$ = 0.

- The third sofa has *cnt*$_{l}$ = 2, *cnt*$_{r}$ = 1, *cnt*$_{t}$ = 1 and *cnt*$_{b}$ = 1.

So the second one corresponds to the given conditions.

In the third example

- The first sofa has *cnt*$_{l}$ = 1, *cnt*$_{r}$ = 1, *cnt*$_{t}$ = 0 and *cnt*$_{b}$ = 1.

- The second sofa has *cnt*$_{l}$ = 1, *cnt*$_{r}$ = 1, *cnt*$_{t}$ = 1 and *cnt*$_{b}$ = 0.

And there is no sofa with the set (1, 0, 0, 0) so the answer is `-1`.

# 沙发小偷

又一轮DecoForces比赛即将到来！Maks爷爷想参加，但有人偷走了他珍贵的沙发！在遭受如此重大的损失后，怎么能表现出色呢？

幸运的是，小偷给Maks爷爷留了一张纸条。这张纸条把Maks带到了沙发仓库。但他仍然不知道哪张沙发属于他，因为它们看起来都一样！

仓库表示为矩阵 *n* × *m*。每张沙发占据两个沿某条边相邻的格子。没有格子被多于一张沙发覆盖。可以有空格子。

如果存在两个这样的格子 *a* 和 *b*，使得 *x*$_{a}$ < *x*$_{b}$，*a* 被 *A* 覆盖且 *b* 被 *B* 覆盖，则称沙发 *A* 位于沙发 *B* 的左边。如果存在两个这样的格子 *a* 和 *b*，使得 *y*$_{a}$ < *y*$_{b}$，*a* 被 *A* 覆盖且 *b* 被 *B* 覆盖，则称沙发 *A* 位于沙发 *B* 的上方。右边和下方的条件以相同方式定义。

注意，在所有条件中 *A* ≠ *B*。此外，某张沙发 *A* 可以既位于另一张沙发 *B* 的上方，又位于它的下方。左边和右边的条件也是如此。

纸条还写道，Maks爷爷的沙发左边有 *cnt*$_{l}$ 张沙发，右边有 *cnt*$_{r}$ 张，上方有 *cnt*$_{t}$ 张，下方有 *cnt*$_{b}$ 张。

Maks爷爷请你帮他找出他的沙发。保证满足给定条件的沙发不超过一张。

输出Maks爷爷的沙发编号。如果不存在满足所有条件的沙发，则输出 `-1`。

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数 *d*（1 ≤ *d* ≤ 10$^{5}$）——仓库中沙发的数量。

第二行包含两个整数 *n*、*m*（1 ≤ *n*、*m* ≤ 10$^{5}$）——仓库的大小。

接下来 *d* 行包含四个整数 *x*$_{1}$、*y*$_{1}$、*x*$_{2}$、*y*$_{2}$（1 ≤ *x*$_{1}$、*x*$_{2}$ ≤ *n*，1 ≤ *y*$_{1}$、*y*$_{2}$ ≤ *m*）——第 *i* 张沙发的坐标。保证格子（*x*$_{1}$，*y*$_{1}$）和（*x*$_{2}$，*y*$_{2}$）有公共边，（*x*$_{1}$，*y*$_{1}$） ≠ （*x*$_{2}$，*y*$_{2}$），且没有格子被多于一张沙发覆盖。

最后一行包含四个整数 *cnt*$_{l}$、*cnt*$_{r}$、*cnt*$_{t}$、*cnt*$_{b}$（0 ≤ *cnt*$_{l}$、*cnt*$_{r}$、*cnt*$_{t}$、*cnt*$_{b}$ ≤ *d* - 1）。

## 输出

打印满足所有条件的沙发的编号。沙发的编号从 1 到 *d*，如输入中所示。如果没有这样的沙发，则打印 `-1`。

## 说明

让我们考虑第二个示例。

- 第一个沙发左边有 0 个，右边有 2 个沙发（(1, 1) 在 (5, 5) 和 (5, 4) 的左边），上方有 0 个，下方有 2 个（第 2 个和第 3 个沙发都在下方）。

- 第二个沙发有 *cnt*$_{l}$ = 2、*cnt*$_{r}$ = 1、*cnt*$_{t}$ = 2 和 *cnt*$_{b}$ = 0。

- 第三个沙发有 *cnt*$_{l}$ = 2、*cnt*$_{r}$ = 1、*cnt*$_{t}$ = 1 和 *cnt*$_{b}$ = 1。

所以第二个沙发符合给定条件。

在第三个示例中

- 第一个沙发有 *cnt*$_{l}$ = 1、*cnt*$_{r}$ = 1、*cnt*$_{t}$ = 0 和 *cnt*$_{b}$ = 1。

- 第二个沙发有 *cnt*$_{l}$ = 1、*cnt*$_{r}$ = 1、*cnt*$_{t}$ = 1 和 *cnt*$_{b}$ = 0。

并且没有沙发的集合为 (1, 0, 0, 0)，所以答案是 `-1`。

# 驾驶考试

波利卡普刚刚尝试通过驾驶考试。他行驶在一条直路上，路上有四种类型的标志。

- 限速：此标志附带一个正整数——标志之后汽车的最高速度（取消之前同类型标志的作用）；

- 允许超车：此标志意味着某辆车遇到它之后，可以超越任何其他车辆；

- 无限速：此标志取消限速（如果有的话）（汽车在此标志之后可以以任意速度行驶）；

- 禁止超车：某辆车在此标志之后不能超越任何其他车辆。

波利卡普依次经过这些标志，每个新标志都会取消之前所有同类标志（限速/超车）的作用。有可能两个或更多“禁止超车”标志一个接一个出现，它们之间没有“允许超车”标志。对于“无限速”和“允许超车”标志也是如此。

在行程开始时，允许超车且没有限速。

给你按时间顺序排列的事件序列——这些事件发生在波利卡普骑行期间。有以下类型的事件：

- 波利卡普将他的车速改变为指定值（此事件附带一个正整数）；

- 波利卡普的车超越了另一辆车；

- 波利卡普的车经过了“限速”标志（此标志附带一个正整数）；

- 波利卡普的车经过了“允许超车”标志；

- 波利卡普的车经过了“无限速”标志；

- 波利卡普的车经过了“禁止超车”标志；

保证按时间顺序的第一个事件是类型1的事件（波利卡普将他的车速改变为指定值）。

考试结束后，波利卡普可以通过告诉驾驶教练他只是没有注意到某些标志来为他的违规行为辩解。波利卡普应该说他没注意到的最少标志数量是多少，以便从他的角度来看他没有违反任何规则？

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数*n*（1 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$）——事件数量。

接下来的*n*行每行以一个整数*t*开头（1 ≤ *t* ≤ 6）——事件的类型。

在第一和第三种类型的查询中，后面跟着一个整数*s*（1 ≤ *s* ≤ 300）（如果它是第一种类型的查询，那么它是波利卡普汽车的新速度；如果它是第三种类型的查询，那么它是新的限速）。

打印 Polycarp 应该说他没注意到的最少道路标志数量，以便从他的角度来看他不会违反任何规则。

在第一个示例中，Polycarp 应该说他没注意到限制为 70 的“限速”标志以及限制为 120 的第二个“限速”标志。

在第二个示例中，Polycarp 没有违反任何规则。

在第三个示例中，Polycarp 应该说他没注意到在“允许超车”标志之后出现的两个“禁止超车”标志。

# 1-2-3

Ilya is working for the company that constructs robots. Ilya writes programs for entertainment robots, and his current project is "Bob", a new-generation game robot. Ilya's boss wants to know his progress so far. Especially he is interested if Bob is better at playing different games than the previous model, "Alice".



So now Ilya wants to compare his robots' performance in a simple game called "1-2-3". This game is similar to the "Rock-Paper-Scissors" game: both robots secretly choose a number from the set {1, 2, 3} and say it at the same moment. If both robots choose the same number, then it's a draw and noone gets any points. But if chosen numbers are different, then one of the robots gets a point: 3 beats 2, 2 beats 1 and 1 beats 3.



Both robots' programs make them choose their numbers in such a way that their choice in (*i* + 1)-th game depends only on the numbers chosen by them in *i*-th game.



Ilya knows that the robots will play *k* games, Alice will choose number *a* in the first game, and Bob will choose *b* in the first game. He also knows both robots' programs and can tell what each robot will choose depending on their choices in previous game. Ilya doesn't want to wait until robots play all *k* games, so he asks you to predict the number of points they will have after the final game.



## Input



The first line contains three numbers *k*, *a*, *b* (1 ≤ *k* ≤ 10$^{18}$, 1 ≤ *a*, *b* ≤ 3).



Then 3 lines follow, *i*-th of them containing 3 numbers *A*$_{i, 1}$, *A*$_{i, 2}$, *A*$_{i, 3}$, where *A*$_{i, j}$ represents Alice's choice in the game if Alice chose *i* in previous game and Bob chose *j* (1 ≤ *A*$_{i, j}$ ≤ 3).



Then 3 lines follow, *i*-th of them containing 3 numbers *B*$_{i, 1}$, *B*$_{i, 2}$, *B*$_{i, 3}$, where *B*$_{i, j}$ represents Bob's choice in the game if Alice chose *i* in previous game and Bob chose *j* (1 ≤ *B*$_{i, j}$ ≤ 3).



## Output



Print two numbers. First of them has to be equal to the number of points Alice will have, and second of them must be Bob's score after *k* games.



## Note



In the second example game goes like this:



![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1e21b6e200707470571d69c9946ace6b56f5279b.png)



The fourth and the seventh game are won by Bob, the first game is draw and the rest are won by Alice.

伊利亚知道机器人将进行 *k* 局游戏，Alice 在第一局中选择数字 *a*，Bob 在第一局中选择 *b*。他还知道两个机器人的程序，并能根据它们在前一局中的选择说出每个机器人将选择什么。伊利亚不想等到机器人玩完所有 *k* 局游戏，所以他请你预测它们在最后一局之后将拥有的分数。

## 输出



打印两个数字。第一个数字必须等于 Alice 将拥有的分数，第二个数字必须是 Bob 在 *k* 局游戏后的分数。

在第二个样例中，游戏过程如下：



![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1e21b6e200707470571d69c9946ace6b56f5279b.png)

# Graphic Settings

Recently Ivan bought a new computer. Excited, he unpacked it and installed his favourite game. With his old computer Ivan had to choose the worst possible graphic settings (because otherwise the framerate would be really low), but now he wants to check, maybe his new computer can perform well even with the best possible graphics?

There are *m* graphics parameters in the game. *i*-th parameter can be set to any positive integer from 1 to *a*$_{i}$, and initially is set to *b*$_{i}$ (*b*$_{i}$ ≤ *a*$_{i}$). So there are ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d17cddb5b1a0e3249ccc45df1ee5a6d7b87bbca4.png) different combinations of parameters. Ivan can increase or decrease any of these parameters by 1; after that the game will be restarted with new parameters (and Ivan will have the opportunity to check chosen combination of parameters).

Ivan wants to try all *p* possible combinations. Also he wants to return to the initial settings after trying all combinations, because he thinks that initial settings can be somehow best suited for his hardware. But Ivan doesn't really want to make a lot of restarts.

So he wants you to tell the following:

- If there exists a way to make exactly *p* changes (each change either decreases or increases some parameter by 1) to try all possible combinations and return to initial combination, then Ivan wants to know this way.

- Otherwise, if there exists a way to make exactly *p* - 1 changes to try all possible combinations (including the initial one), then Ivan wants to know this way.

Help Ivan by showing him the way to change parameters!

## Input

The first line of input contains one integer number *m* (1 ≤ *m* ≤ 6).

The second line contains *m* integer numbers *a*$_{1}$, *a*$_{2}$, ..., *a*$_{m}$ (2 ≤ *a*$_{i}$ ≤ 1000). It is guaranteed that ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0ada6082392fb845829961539792ec286cdb5a27.png).

The third line contains *m* integer numbers *b*$_{1}$, *b*$_{2}$, ..., *b*$_{m}$ (1 ≤ *b*$_{i}$ ≤ *a*$_{i}$).

## Output

If there is a way to make exactly *p* changes (each change either decreases or increases some parameter by 1) to try all possible combinations and return to initial combination, then output `Cycle` in the first line. Then *p* lines must follow, each desribing a change. The line must be either `inc x` (increase parameter *x* by 1) or `dec x` (decrease it).

Otherwise, if there is a way to make exactly *p* - 1 changes to try all possible combinations (including the initial one), then output `Path` in the first line. Then *p* - 1 lines must follow, each describing the change the same way as mentioned above.

Otherwise, output `No`.

# 图形设置

最近 Ivan 买了一台新电脑。他兴奋地拆开包装并安装了他最喜欢的游戏。用旧电脑时，Ivan 不得不选择最差的画质设置（因为否则帧率会非常低），但现在他想看看，也许他的新电脑即使使用最好的画质也能运行得很好？

游戏中有 *m* 个图形参数。第 *i* 个参数可以设置为从 1 到 *a*$_{i}$ 的任意正整数，并且初始设置为 *b*$_{i}$（*b*$_{i}$ ≤ *a*$_{i}$）。因此共有 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d17cddb5b1a0e3249ccc45df1ee5a6d7b87bbca4.png) 种不同的参数组合。Ivan 可以将其中任意一个参数增加或减少 1；之后游戏将以新的参数重新启动（并且 Ivan 将有机会检查所选的参数组合）。

伊万想尝试所有 *p* 种可能的组合。此外，他希望在尝试完所有组合后回到初始设置，因为他认为初始设置可能最适合他的硬件。但伊万并不真的想进行大量重启。

所以他希望你回答以下内容：

- 如果存在一种方法，恰好进行 *p* 次更改（每次更改将某个参数减少或增加 1），以尝试所有可能的组合并返回初始组合，那么 Ivan 想知道这种方法。

- 否则，如果存在一种方法，恰好进行 *p* - 1 次修改来尝试所有可能的组合（包括初始组合），那么 Ivan 想知道这种方法。

请通过向伊万展示更改参数的方法来帮助他！

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 *m*（1 ≤ *m* ≤ 6）。

第二行包含 *m* 个整数 *a*$_{1}$，*a*$_{2}$，……，*a*$_{m}$（2 ≤ *a*$_{i}$ ≤ 1000）。保证 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0ada6082392fb845829961539792ec286cdb5a27.png)。

第三行包含 *m* 个整数 *b*$_{1}$、*b*$_{2}$、……、*b*$_{m}$（1 ≤ *b*$_{i}$ ≤ *a*$_{i}$）。

## ## 题目描述

给定一个长度为 \(2n\) 的数组 \(a\)，其中 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

我们称一个数对 \((i,j)\)（\(1 \le i < j \le 2n\)）是“好对”，当且仅当 \(a_i = a_j\)，且区间 \([i,j]\) 中不存在两个相同的数。

请求出好对的数量。

## 输入格式

第一行一个整数 \(n\)（\(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\)）。

第二行 \(2n\) 个整数 \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2n}\)（\(1 \le a_i \le n\)），保证 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

## 输出格式

输出一行一个整数，表示好对的数量。

## 样例输入 1

```
3
1 2 1 3 2 3
```

## 样例输出 1

```
2
```

## 样例解释 1

好对为 \((1,3)\) 和 \((2,5)\)。注意 \((4,6)\) 不是好对，因为区间 \([4,6]\) 中 \(3\) 出现了两次。

## 样例输入 2

```
1
1 1
```

## 样例输出 2

```
1
```

## 样例解释 2

唯一的好对为 \((1,2)\)。

## 约束

- \(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\)
- \(1 \le a_i \le n\)
- \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

如果存在一种方法，恰好进行 *p* 次更改（每次更改将某个参数增加或减少 1），以尝试所有可能的组合并返回初始组合，则在第一行输出 `Cycle`。随后必须跟随 *p* 行，每行描述一次更改。该行必须是 `inc x`（将参数 *x* 增加 1）或 `dec x`（将其减少）。

否则，如果存在一种方法，恰好进行 *p* - 1 次更改来尝试所有可能的组合（包括初始组合），则在第一行输出 `Path`。随后必须跟随 *p* - 1 行，每行按照上述相同方式描述一次更改。

否则，输出 `No`。

# Chores

Luba has to do *n* chores today. *i*-th chore takes *a*$_{i}$ units of time to complete. It is guaranteed that for every ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/33efc769667118b03a335770b969c3a335b55f01.png) the condition *a*$_{i}$ ≥ *a*$_{i - 1}$ is met, so the sequence is sorted.

Also Luba can work really hard on some chores. She can choose not more than *k* any chores and do each of them in *x* units of time instead of *a*$_{i}$ (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6920e94f798823d25de0307d3d79fea4434bb5ec.png)).

Luba is very responsible, so she has to do all *n* chores, and now she wants to know the minimum time she needs to do everything. Luba cannot do two chores simultaneously.

## Input

The first line contains three integers *n*, *k*, *x* (1 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* ≤ 100, 1 ≤ *x* ≤ 99) — the number of chores Luba has to do, the number of chores she can do in *x* units of time, and the number *x* itself.

The second line contains *n* integer numbers *a*$_{i}$ (2 ≤ *a*$_{i}$ ≤ 100) — the time Luba has to spend to do *i*-th chore.

It is guaranteed that ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6920e94f798823d25de0307d3d79fea4434bb5ec.png), and for each ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/33efc769667118b03a335770b969c3a335b55f01.png) *a*$_{i}$ ≥ *a*$_{i - 1}$.

## Output

Print one number — minimum time Luba needs to do all *n* chores.

## Note

In the first example the best option would be to do the third and the fourth chore, spending *x* = 2 time on each instead of *a*$_{3}$ and *a*$_{4}$, respectively. Then the answer is 3 + 6 + 2 + 2 = 13.

In the second example Luba can choose any two chores to spend *x* time on them instead of *a*$_{i}$. So the answer is 100·3 + 2·1 = 302.

# Merge Sort

Merge sort is a well-known sorting algorithm. The main function that sorts the elements of array *a* with indices from [*l*, *r*) can be implemented as follows:

- If the segment [*l*, *r*) is already sorted in non-descending order (that is, for any *i* such that *l* ≤ *i* < *r* - 1 *a*[*i*] ≤ *a*[*i* + 1]), then end the function call;

- Let ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/605fe3f9e91c8128533aea46c712d4e485918a63.png);

- Call *mergesort*(*a*, *l*, *mid*);

- Call *mergesort*(*a*, *mid*, *r*);

- Merge segments [*l*, *mid*) and [*mid*, *r*), making the segment [*l*, *r*) sorted in non-descending order. The merge algorithm doesn't call any other functions.

The array in this problem is 0-indexed, so to sort the whole array, you need to call *mergesort*(*a*, 0, *n*).

The number of calls of function *mergesort* is very important, so Ivan has decided to calculate it while sorting the array. For example, if *a* = {1, 2, 3, 4}, then there will be 1 call of *mergesort* — *mergesort*(0, 4), which will check that the array is sorted and then end. If *a* = {2, 1, 3}, then the number of calls is 3: first of all, you call *mergesort*(0, 3), which then sets *mid* = 1 and calls *mergesort*(0, 1) and *mergesort*(1, 3), which do not perform any recursive calls because segments (0, 1) and (1, 3) are sorted.

Ivan has implemented the program that counts the number of *mergesort* calls, but now he needs to test it. To do this, he needs to find an array *a* such that *a* is a permutation of size *n* (that is, the number of elements in *a* is *n*, and every integer number from [1, *n*] can be found in this array), and the number of *mergesort* calls when sorting the array is exactly *k*.

Help Ivan to find an array he wants!

## Input

The first line contains two numbers *n* and *k* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100000, 1 ≤ *k* ≤ 200000) — the size of a desired permutation and the number of *mergesort* calls required to sort it.

## Output

If a permutation of size *n* such that there will be exactly *k* calls of *mergesort* while sorting it doesn't exist, output  - 1. Otherwise output *n* integer numbers *a*[0], *a*[1], ..., *a*[*n* - 1] — the elements of a permutation that would meet the required conditions. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.

# 归并排序

归并排序是一种著名的排序算法。对数组 *a* 中下标范围为 [*l*, *r*) 的元素进行排序的主函数可以实现如下：

- 如果线段[*l*, *r*)已经按非降序排好序（即对于任意满足*l* ≤ *i* < *r* - 1的*i*，都有*a*[*i*] ≤ *a*[*i* + 1]），则结束该函数调用；

- 设 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/605fe3f9e91c8128533aea46c712d4e485918a63.png)；

- 调用*mergesort*(*a*, *l*, *mid*)；

- 调用 *mergesort*(*a*, *mid*, *r*)；

- 合并区间[*l*, *mid*)和[*mid*, *r*)，使区间[*l*, *r*)按非降序排列。该合并算法不调用任何其他函数。

本题中的数组采用 0 索引，因此要对整个数组排序，需要调用 *mergesort*(*a*, 0, *n*)。

函数 *mergesort* 的调用次数非常重要，因此 Ivan 决定在排序数组时计算它。例如，如果 *a* = {1, 2, 3, 4}，那么将有 1 次 *mergesort* 调用——*mergesort*(0, 4)，它会检查数组是否已排序，然后结束。如果 *a* = {2, 1, 3}，那么调用次数为 3：首先，你调用 *mergesort*(0, 3)，然后它设置 *mid* = 1 并调用 *mergesort*(0, 1) 和 *mergesort*(1, 3)，这两个调用不执行任何递归调用，因为区间 (0, 1) 和 (1, 3) 已排序。

Ivan 已经实现了统计 *mergesort* 调用次数的程序，但现在他需要测试它。为此，他需要找到一个数组 *a*，使得 *a* 是大小为 *n* 的排列（即 *a* 中元素个数为 *n*，且 [1, *n*] 中的每个整数都能在这个数组中找到），并且排序该数组时 *mergesort* 的调用次数恰好为 *k*。

帮助伊万找到他想要的数组！

## 输入

第一行包含两个数 *n* 和 *k*（1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100000，1 ≤ *k* ≤ 200000）——所需排列的大小以及对其进行排序所需的 *mergesort* 调用次数。

# The Modcrab

Vova is again playing some computer game, now an RPG. In the game Vova's character received a quest: to slay the fearsome monster called Modcrab.

After two hours of playing the game Vova has tracked the monster and analyzed its tactics. The Modcrab has *h*$_{2}$ health points and an attack power of *a*$_{2}$. Knowing that, Vova has decided to buy a lot of strong healing potions and to prepare for battle.

Vova's character has *h*$_{1}$ health points and an attack power of *a*$_{1}$. Also he has a large supply of healing potions, each of which increases his current amount of health points by *c*$_{1}$ when Vova drinks a potion. All potions are identical to each other. It is guaranteed that *c*$_{1}$ > *a*$_{2}$.

The battle consists of multiple phases. In the beginning of each phase, Vova can either attack the monster (thus reducing its health by *a*$_{1}$) or drink a healing potion (it increases Vova's health by *c*$_{1}$; Vova's health can exceed *h*$_{1}$). Then, if the battle is not over yet, the Modcrab attacks Vova, reducing his health by *a*$_{2}$. The battle ends when Vova's (or Modcrab's) health drops to 0 or lower. It is possible that the battle ends in a middle of a phase after Vova's attack.

Of course, Vova wants to win the fight. But also he wants to do it as fast as possible. So he wants to make up a strategy that will allow him to win the fight after the minimum possible number of phases.

Help Vova to make up a strategy! You may assume that Vova never runs out of healing potions, and that he can always win.

## Input

The first line contains three integers *h*$_{1}$, *a*$_{1}$, *c*$_{1}$ (1 ≤ *h*$_{1}$, *a*$_{1}$ ≤ 100, 2 ≤ *c*$_{1}$ ≤ 100) — Vova's health, Vova's attack power and the healing power of a potion.

The second line contains two integers *h*$_{2}$, *a*$_{2}$ (1 ≤ *h*$_{2}$ ≤ 100, 1 ≤ *a*$_{2}$ < *c*$_{1}$) — the Modcrab's health and his attack power.

## Output

In the first line print one integer *n* denoting the minimum number of phases required to win the battle.

Then print *n* lines. *i*-th line must be equal to `HEAL` if Vova drinks a potion in *i*-th phase, or `STRIKE` if he attacks the Modcrab.

The strategy must be valid: Vova's character must not be defeated before slaying the Modcrab, and the monster's health must be 0 or lower after Vova's last action.

If there are multiple optimal solutions, print any of them.

## Note

In the first example Vova's character must heal before or after his first attack. Otherwise his health will drop to zero in 2 phases while he needs 3 strikes to win.

In the second example no healing needed, two strikes are enough to get monster to zero health and win with 6 health left.

# Yet Another Maxflow Problem

In this problem you will have to deal with a very special network.

The network consists of two parts: part *A* and part *B*. Each part consists of *n* vertices; *i*-th vertex of part *A* is denoted as *A*$_{i}$, and *i*-th vertex of part *B* is denoted as *B*$_{i}$.

For each index *i* (1 ≤ *i* < *n*) there is a directed edge from vertex *A*$_{i}$ to vertex *A*$_{i + 1}$, and from *B*$_{i}$ to *B*$_{i + 1}$, respectively. Capacities of these edges are given in the input. Also there might be several directed edges going from part *A* to part *B* (but never from *B* to *A*).

You have to calculate the [maximum flow value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_flow_problem) from *A*$_{1}$ to *B*$_{n}$ in this network. Capacities of edges connecting *A*$_{i}$ to *A*$_{i + 1}$ might sometimes change, and you also have to maintain the maximum flow value after these changes. Apart from that, the network is fixed (there are no changes in part *B*, no changes of edges going from *A* to *B*, and no edge insertions or deletions).

Take a look at the example and the notes to understand the structure of the network better.

## Input

The first line contains three integer numbers *n*, *m* and *q* (2 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$, 0 ≤ *q* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$) — the number of vertices in each part, the number of edges going from *A* to *B* and the number of changes, respectively.

Then *n* - 1 lines follow, *i*-th line contains two integers *x*$_{i}$ and *y*$_{i}$ denoting that the edge from *A*$_{i}$ to *A*$_{i + 1}$ has capacity *x*$_{i}$ and the edge from *B*$_{i}$ to *B*$_{i + 1}$ has capacity *y*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *x*$_{i}$, *y*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{9}$).

Then *m* lines follow, describing the edges from *A* to *B*. Each line contains three integers *x*, *y* and *z* denoting an edge from *A*$_{x}$ to *B*$_{y}$ with capacity *z* (1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n*, 1 ≤ *z* ≤ 10$^{9}$). There might be multiple edges from *A*$_{x}$ to *B*$_{y}$.

And then *q* lines follow, describing a sequence of changes to the network. *i*-th line contains two integers *v*$_{i}$ and *w*$_{i}$, denoting that the capacity of the edge from *A*$_{vi}$ to *A*$_{vi + 1}$ is set to *w*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *v*$_{i}$ < *n*, 1 ≤ *w*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{9}$).

## Output

Firstly, print the maximum flow value in the original network. Then print *q* integers, *i*-th of them must be equal to the maximum flow value after *i*-th change.

## Note

This is the original network in the example:

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2cde6a73d42b3f76712d52ebfe4f6441bc5dc343.png)

# 又一个最大流问题

在这个问题中，你将需要处理一个非常特殊的网络。

该网络由两部分组成：部分 *A* 和部分 *B*。每个部分由 *n* 个顶点组成；部分 *A* 的第 *i* 个顶点记为 *A*$_{i}$，部分 *B* 的第 *i* 个顶点记为 *B*$_{i}$。

对于每个索引 *i*（1 ≤ *i* < *n*），分别存在一条从顶点 *A*$_{i}$ 到顶点 *A*$_{i + 1}$ 的有向边，以及一条从 *B*$_{i}$ 到 *B*$_{i + 1}$ 的有向边。这些边的容量在输入中给出。此外，可能存在若干条从部分 *A* 指向部分 *B* 的有向边（但绝不存在从 *B* 指向 *A* 的边）。

你需要计算该网络中从 *A*$_{1}$ 到 *B*$_{n}$ 的[最大流值](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_flow_problem)。连接 *A*$_{i}$ 到 *A*$_{i + 1}$ 的边的容量有时会发生变化，并且你还需要在这些变化后维护最大流值。除此之外，网络是固定的（*B* 部分没有变化，从 *A* 到 *B* 的边没有变化，也没有边的插入或删除）。

看看示例和注释，以便更好地理解网络的结构。

## 输入

第一行包含三个整数 *n*、*m* 和 *q*（2 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$，0 ≤ *q* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$）——分别是每一部分的顶点数、从 *A* 到 *B* 的边数以及更改次数。

接下来是 *n* - 1 行，第 *i* 行包含两个整数 *x*$_{i}$ 和 *y*$_{i}$，表示从 *A*$_{i}$ 到 *A*$_{i + 1}$ 的边容量为 *x*$_{i}$，从 *B*$_{i}$ 到 *B*$_{i + 1}$ 的边容量为 *y*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *x*$_{i}$，*y*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{9}$）。

接下来是 *m* 行，描述从 *A* 到 *B* 的边。每行包含三个整数 *x*、*y* 和 *z*，表示一条从 *A*$_{x}$ 到 *B*$_{y}$ 的边，容量为 *z*（1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n*，1 ≤ *z* ≤ 10$^{9}$）。从 *A*$_{x}$ 到 *B*$_{y}$ 可能存在多条边。

接下来是 *q* 行，描述对网络的一系列更改。第 *i* 行包含两个整数 *v*$_{i}$ 和 *w*$_{i}$，表示从 *A*$_{vi}$ 到 *A*$_{vi + 1}$ 的边的容量被设为 *w*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *v*$_{i}$ < *n*，1 ≤ *w*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{9}$）。

## 输出

首先，输出原始网络中的最大流值。然后输出 *q* 个整数，其中第 *i* 个必须等于第 *i* 次修改后的最大流值。

# Stack Sorting

Let's suppose you have an array *a*, a stack *s* (initially empty) and an array *b* (also initially empty).

You may perform the following operations until both *a* and *s* are empty:

- Take the first element of *a*, push it into *s* and remove it from *a* (if *a* is not empty);

- Take the top element from *s*, append it to the end of array *b* and remove it from *s* (if *s* is not empty).

You can perform these operations in arbitrary order.

If there exists a way to perform the operations such that array *b* is sorted in non-descending order in the end, then array *a* is called stack-sortable.

For example, [3, 1, 2] is stack-sortable, because *b* will be sorted if we perform the following operations:

- Remove 3 from *a* and push it into *s*;

- Remove 1 from *a* and push it into *s*;

- Remove 1 from *s* and append it to the end of *b*;

- Remove 2 from *a* and push it into *s*;

- Remove 2 from *s* and append it to the end of *b*;

- Remove 3 from *s* and append it to the end of *b*.

After all these operations *b* = [1, 2, 3], so [3, 1, 2] is stack-sortable. [2, 3, 1] is not stack-sortable.

You are given *k* first elements of some permutation *p* of size *n* (recall that a permutation of size *n* is an array of size *n* where each integer from 1 to *n* occurs exactly once). You have to restore the remaining *n* - *k* elements of this permutation so it is stack-sortable. If there are multiple answers, choose the answer such that *p* is lexicographically maximal (an array *q* is lexicographically greater than an array *p* iff there exists some integer *k* such that for every *i* < *k* *q*$_{i}$ = *p*$_{i}$, and *q*$_{k}$ > *p*$_{k}$). You may not swap or change any of first *k* elements of the permutation.

Print the lexicographically maximal permutation *p* you can obtain.

If there exists no answer then output `-1`.

## Input

The first line contains two integers *n* and *k* (2 ≤ *n* ≤ 200000, 1 ≤ *k* < *n*) — the size of a desired permutation, and the number of elements you are given, respectively.

The second line contains *k* integers *p*$_{1}$, *p*$_{2}$, ..., *p*$_{k}$ (1 ≤ *p*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*) — the first *k* elements of *p*. These integers are pairwise distinct.

## Output

If it is possible to restore a stack-sortable permutation *p* of size *n* such that the first *k* elements of *p* are equal to elements given in the input, print lexicographically maximal such permutation.

Otherwise print `-1`.

# 栈排序

假设你有一个数组 *a*、一个栈 *s*（初始为空）和一个数组 *b*（同样初始为空）。

你可以执行以下操作，直到 *a* 和 *s* 都为空：

- 取 *a* 的第一个元素，将其压入 *s* 并从 *a* 中移除（如果 *a* 不为空）；

- 取 *s* 的栈顶元素，将其追加到数组 *b* 的末尾并从 *s* 中移除（如果 *s* 不为空）。

你可以以任意顺序执行这些操作。

如果存在一种执行操作的方式，使得最终数组 *b* 按非降序排序，那么数组 *a* 被称为栈可排序的。

例如，[3, 1, 2] 是栈可排序的，因为如果我们执行以下操作，*b* 将是有序的：

- 从 *a* 中移除 3 并将其压入 *s*；

- 从 *a* 中移除 1 并将其压入 *s*；

- 从 *s* 中移除 1 并将其追加到 *b* 的末尾；

- 从 *a* 中移除 2 并将其压入 *s*；

- 从 *s* 中移除 2 并将其追加到 *b* 的末尾；

- 从 *s* 中移除 3 并将其追加到 *b* 的末尾。

经过所有这些操作后 *b* = [1, 2, 3]，所以 [3, 1, 2] 是栈可排序的。[2, 3, 1] 不是栈可排序的。

给定大小为 *n* 的某个排列 *p* 的前 *k* 个元素（回忆一下，大小为 *n* 的排列是一个大小为 *n* 的数组，其中从 1 到 *n* 的每个整数恰好出现一次）。你必须恢复这个排列剩余的 *n* - *k* 个元素，使其是栈可排序的。如果有多个答案，选择使 *p* 字典序最大的答案（数组 *q* 字典序大于数组 *p* 当且仅当存在某个整数 *k*，使得对于每个 *i* < *k* 都有 *q*$_{i}$ = *p*$_{i}$，且 *q*$_{k}$ > *p*$_{k}$）。你不能交换或改变排列的前 *k* 个元素中的任何一个。

输出你能得到的字典序最大的排列 *p*。

如果不存在答案，则输出 `-1`。

## 输入

第一行包含两个整数 *n* 和 *k*（2 ≤ *n* ≤ 200000，1 ≤ *k* < *n*）——分别表示所需排列的大小和你已给定的元素个数。

第二行包含 *k* 个整数 *p*$_{1}$, *p*$_{2}$, ..., *p*$_{k}$（1 ≤ *p*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*）——即 *p* 的前 *k* 个元素。这些整数两两不同。

## 输出

如果能够还原出一个大小为 *n* 的栈可排序排列 *p*，使得 *p* 的前 *k* 个元素等于输入中给出的元素，则输出字典序最大的这样的排列。

否则输出 `-1`。

# Water The Garden

It is winter now, and Max decided it's about time he watered the garden.



The garden can be represented as *n* consecutive garden beds, numbered from 1 to *n*. *k* beds contain water taps (*i*-th tap is located in the bed *x*$_{i}$), which, if turned on, start delivering water to neighbouring beds. If the tap on the bed *x*$_{i}$ is turned on, then after one second has passed, the bed *x*$_{i}$ will be watered; after two seconds have passed, the beds from the segment [*x*$_{i}$ - 1, *x*$_{i}$ + 1] will be watered (if they exist); after *j* seconds have passed (*j* is an integer number), the beds from the segment [*x*$_{i}$ - (*j* - 1), *x*$_{i}$ + (*j* - 1)] will be watered (if they exist). Nothing changes during the seconds, so, for example, we can't say that the segment [*x*$_{i}$ - 2.5, *x*$_{i}$ + 2.5] will be watered after 2.5 seconds have passed; only the segment [*x*$_{i}$ - 2, *x*$_{i}$ + 2] will be watered at that moment.

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b708fecdfb8d8ab53a19865ec9979981caf68a46.png) The garden from test 1. White colour denotes a garden bed without a tap, red colour — a garden bed with a tap.  ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ed40706bef97707f5a0b1d41b49f2a34f16de9c3.png) The garden from test 1 after 2 seconds have passed after turning on the tap. White colour denotes an unwatered garden bed, blue colour — a watered bed. 

Max wants to turn on all the water taps at the same moment, and now he wonders, what is the minimum number of seconds that have to pass after he turns on some taps until the whole garden is watered. Help him to find the answer!



## Input



The first line contains one integer *t* — the number of test cases to solve (1 ≤ *t* ≤ 200).



Then *t* test cases follow. The first line of each test case contains two integers *n* and *k* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200, 1 ≤ *k* ≤ *n*) — the number of garden beds and water taps, respectively.



Next line contains *k* integers *x*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *x*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*) — the location of *i*-th water tap. It is guaranteed that for each ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe03c352479a1f92e4a3d577006ed0f1fff0ee43.png) condition *x*$_{i - 1}$ < *x*$_{i}$ holds.



It is guaranteed that the sum of *n* over all test cases doesn't exceed 200.



Note that in hacks you have to set *t* = 1.



## Output



For each test case print one integer — the minimum number of seconds that have to pass after Max turns on some of the water taps, until the whole garden is watered.



## Note



The first example consists of 3 tests:



- There are 5 garden beds, and a water tap in the bed 3. If we turn it on, then after 1 second passes, only bed 3 will be watered; after 2 seconds pass, beds [1, 3] will be watered, and after 3 seconds pass, everything will be watered.

- There are 3 garden beds, and there is a water tap in each one. If we turn all of them on, then everything will be watered after 1 second passes.

- There are 4 garden beds, and only one tap in the bed 1. It will take 4 seconds to water, for example, bed 4.

# 浇灌花园

现在是冬天，Max 觉得是时候浇灌花园了。



花园可以表示为 *n* 个连续的花坛，编号从 1 到 *n*。其中 *k* 个花坛装有水龙头（第 *i* 个水龙头位于花坛 *x*$_{i}$），如果打开，就会开始向相邻的花坛供水。如果打开位于花坛 *x*$_{i}$ 的水龙头，那么经过一秒后，花坛 *x*$_{i}$ 会被浇灌；经过两秒后，区间 [*x*$_{i}$ - 1, *x*$_{i}$ + 1] 内的花坛会被浇灌（如果存在）；经过 *j* 秒后（*j* 是整数），区间 [*x*$_{i}$ - (*j* - 1), *x*$_{i}$ + (*j* - 1)] 内的花坛会被浇灌（如果存在）。在秒内不会发生其他变化，因此，例如，我们不能说经过 2.5 秒后区间 [*x*$_{i}$ - 2.5, *x*$_{i}$ + 2.5] 会被浇灌；在那个时刻只有区间 [*x*$_{i}$ - 2, *x*$_{i}$ + 2] 会被浇灌。

 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b708fecdfb8d8ab53a19865ec9979981caf68a46.png) 测试 1 中的花园。白色表示没有水龙头的花坛，红色表示有水龙头的花坛。  ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ed40706bef97707f5a0b1d41b49f2a34f16de9c3.png) 测试 1 中的花园在打开水龙头后经过 2 秒。白色表示未浇灌的花坛，蓝色表示已浇灌的花坛。 

Max 想在同一时刻打开所有水龙头，现在他想知道，在他打开一些水龙头后，至少需要经过多少秒，整个花园才会被浇灌。帮助他找到答案！

# Tea Queue

Recently *n* students from city S moved to city P to attend a programming camp.

They moved there by train. In the evening, all students in the train decided that they want to drink some tea. Of course, no two people can use the same teapot simultaneously, so the students had to form a queue to get their tea.

*i*-th student comes to the end of the queue at the beginning of *l*$_{i}$-th second. If there are multiple students coming to the queue in the same moment, then the student with greater index comes after the student with lesser index. Students in the queue behave as follows: if there is nobody in the queue before the student, then he uses the teapot for exactly one second and leaves the queue with his tea; otherwise the student waits for the people before him to get their tea. If at the beginning of *r*$_{i}$-th second student *i* still cannot get his tea (there is someone before him in the queue), then he leaves the queue without getting any tea.

For each student determine the second he will use the teapot and get his tea (if he actually gets it).

## Input

The first line contains one integer *t* — the number of test cases to solve (1 ≤ *t* ≤ 1000).

Then *t* test cases follow. The first line of each test case contains one integer *n* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000) — the number of students.

Then *n* lines follow. Each line contains two integer *l*$_{i}$, *r*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *l*$_{i}$ ≤ *r*$_{i}$ ≤ 5000) — the second *i*-th student comes to the end of the queue, and the second he leaves the queue if he still cannot get his tea.

It is guaranteed that for every ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/05362455b6ad5b6870bcef95c0b20ccb40cc3532.png) condition *l*$_{i - 1}$ ≤ *l*$_{i}$ holds.

The sum of *n* over all test cases doesn't exceed 1000.

Note that in hacks you have to set *t* = 1.

## Output

For each test case print *n* integers. *i*-th of them must be equal to the second when *i*-th student gets his tea, or 0 if he leaves without tea.

## Note

The example contains 2 tests:

- During 1-st second, students 1 and 2 come to the queue, and student 1 gets his tea. Student 2 gets his tea during 2-nd second.

- During 1-st second, students 1 and 2 come to the queue, student 1 gets his tea, and student 2 leaves without tea. During 2-nd second, student 3 comes and gets his tea.

# 茶队列

最近，来自城市 S 的 *n* 名学生搬到了城市 P，参加一个编程训练营。

他们乘火车到了那里。晚上，火车上的所有学生都决定要喝点茶。当然，不能有两个人同时使用同一个茶壶，所以学生们不得不排成一队来取茶。

第 *i* 个学生在第 *l*$_{i}$ 秒初来到队尾。如果同一时刻有多个学生来到队列，则编号较大的学生排在编号较小的学生之后。队列中的学生行为如下：如果该学生前面没有人，那么他恰好使用茶壶一秒，然后带着茶离开队列；否则该学生等待前面的人拿到茶。如果在第 *r*$_{i}$ 秒初，学生 *i* 仍然无法拿到茶（他前面还有人），那么他没有拿到任何茶就离开队列。

对每位学生，确定他将使用茶壶并拿到茶（如果他确实拿到了）的那一秒。

## 输入

接下来有 *t* 个测试用例。每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 *n*（1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000）——学生人数。

接下来有 *n* 行。每行包含两个整数 *l*$_{i}$、*r*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *l*$_{i}$ ≤ *r*$_{i}$ ≤ 5000）——第 *i* 个学生第二次来到队尾，并且如果他仍然拿不到他的茶，他第二次离开队列。

所有测试用例中 *n* 的总和不超过 1000。

给定一个长度为 \(2n\) 的数组 \(a\)，其中 \(1\) 到 \(n\) 每个整数恰好出现两次。

我们称一个数对 \((i,j)\)（\(1 \le i < j \le 2n\)）是“好对”，当且仅当 \(a_i = a_j\)，且区间 \([i,j]\) 中不存在两个相同的数。

第一行一个整数 \(n\)（\(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\)）。

## 样例输入 1

```

1 2 1 3 2 3

## 样例输出 1

```
2

## 样例解释 1

好对为 \((1,3)\) 和 \((2,5)\)。注意 \((4,6)\) 不是好对，因为区间 \([4,6]\) 中 \(3\) 出现了两次。

1

1

唯一的好对为 \((1,2)\)。

- \(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\)
- \(1 \le a_i \le n\)

对于每个测试用例，输出 *n* 个整数。其中第 *i* 个数必须等于第 *i* 名学生拿到茶的时间，或者如果他没拿到茶就离开，则为 0。

# Matrix Walk

There is a matrix *A* of size *x* × *y* filled with integers. For every ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e87325918316c52884e4063f23cf77cfe475ee7c.png), ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b2547b0e9acdacd0f9e1ca13295a4cc301cde743.png) *A*$_{i, j}$ = *y*(*i* - 1) + *j*. Obviously, every integer from [1..*xy*] occurs exactly once in this matrix.

You have traversed some path in this matrix. Your path can be described as a sequence of visited cells *a*$_{1}$, *a*$_{2}$, ..., *a*$_{n}$ denoting that you started in the cell containing the number *a*$_{1}$, then moved to the cell with the number *a*$_{2}$, and so on.

From the cell located in *i*-th line and *j*-th column (we denote this cell as (*i*, *j*)) you can move into one of the following cells:

- (*i* + 1, *j*) — only if *i* < *x*;

- (*i*, *j* + 1) — only if *j* < *y*;

- (*i* - 1, *j*) — only if *i* > 1;

- (*i*, *j* - 1) — only if *j* > 1.

Notice that making a move requires you to go to an adjacent cell. It is not allowed to stay in the same cell. You don't know *x* and *y* exactly, but you have to find any possible values for these numbers such that you could start in the cell containing the integer *a*$_{1}$, then move to the cell containing *a*$_{2}$ (in one step), then move to the cell containing *a*$_{3}$ (also in one step) and so on. Can you choose *x* and *y* so that they don't contradict with your sequence of moves?

## Input

The first line contains one integer number *n* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200000) — the number of cells you visited on your path (if some cell is visited twice, then it's listed twice).

The second line contains *n* integers *a*$_{1}$, *a*$_{2}$, ..., *a*$_{n}$ (1 ≤ *a*$_{i}$ ≤ 10$^{9}$) — the integers in the cells on your path.

## Output

If all possible values of *x* and *y* such that 1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 10$^{9}$ contradict with the information about your path, print `NO`.

Otherwise, print `YES` in the first line, and in the second line print the values *x* and *y* such that your path was possible with such number of lines and columns in the matrix. Remember that they must be positive integers not exceeding 10$^{9}$.

## Note

The matrix and the path on it in the first test looks like this:

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/190a823a508d8dcf4bd86277a5f22b80210849c6.png)

Also there exist multiple correct answers for both the first and the third examples.

# Tufurama

有一天，Polycarp 决定重温他最喜欢的著名电视剧《Tufurama》中的一集。当他用搜索查询“Watch Tufurama season 3 episode 7 online full hd free”却只得到第 7 季第 3 集的结果时，他非常惊讶。这让 Polycarp 感到困惑——如果他某天决定重温整部剧，却找不到正确的剧集来看怎么办？Polycarp 现在想统计他被迫用某种不同方法搜索某一集的次数。

电视剧有 *n* 季（编号从 1 到 *n*），第 *i* 季有 *a*$_{i}$ 集（编号从 1 到 *a*$_{i}$）。Polycarp 认为，如果存在一对整数 *x* 和 *y*（*x* < *y*），使得第 *x* 季第 *y* 集和第 *y* 季第 *x* 集都存在，那么其中一个搜索查询就会包含错误的结果。请帮助 Polycarp 计算这样的数对数量！

# Byteland, Berland and Disputed Cities

The cities of Byteland and Berland are located on the axis $$$Ox$$$. In addition, on this axis there are also disputed cities, which belong to each of the countries in their opinion. Thus, on the line $$$Ox$$$ there are three types of cities:

- the cities of Byteland,

- the cities of Berland,

- disputed cities.

Recently, the project BNET has been launched — a computer network of a new generation. Now the task of the both countries is to connect the cities so that the network of this country is connected.

The countries agreed to connect the pairs of cities with BNET cables in such a way that:

- If you look at the only cities of Byteland and the disputed cities, then in the resulting set of cities, any city should be reachable from any other one by one or more cables,

- If you look at the only cities of Berland and the disputed cities, then in the resulting set of cities, any city should be reachable from any other one by one or more cables.

Thus, it is necessary to choose a set of pairs of cities to connect by cables in such a way that both conditions are satisfied simultaneously. Cables allow bi-directional data transfer. Each cable connects exactly two distinct cities.

The cost of laying a cable from one city to another is equal to the distance between them. Find the minimum total cost of laying a set of cables so that two subsets of cities (Byteland and disputed cities, Berland and disputed cities) are connected.

Each city is a point on the line $$$Ox$$$. It is technically possible to connect the cities $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ with a cable so that the city $$$c$$$ ($$$a \lt c \lt b$$$) is not connected to this cable, where $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$ and $$$c$$$ are simultaneously coordinates of the cities $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$ and $$$c$$$.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^{5}$$$) — the number of cities.

The following $$$n$$$ lines contains an integer $$$x_i$$$ and the letter $$$c_i$$$ ($$$-10^{9} \le x_i \le 10^{9}$$$) — the coordinate of the city and its type. If the city belongs to Byteland, $$$c_i$$$ equals to '`B`'. If the city belongs to Berland, $$$c_i$$$ equals to «`R`». If the city is disputed, $$$c_i$$$ equals to '`P`'.

All cities have distinct coordinates. Guaranteed, that the cities are given in the increasing order of their coordinates.

## Output

Print the minimal total length of such set of cables, that if we delete all Berland cities ($$$c_i$$$='`R`'), it will be possible to find a way from any remaining city to any other remaining city, moving only by cables. Similarly, if we delete all Byteland cities ($$$c_i$$$='`B`'), it will be possible to find a way from any remaining city to any other remaining city, moving only by cables.

## Note

In the first example, you should connect the first city with the second, the second with the third, and the third with the fourth. The total length of the cables will be $$$5 + 3 + 4 = 12$$$.

In the second example there are no disputed cities, so you need to connect all the neighboring cities of Byteland and all the neighboring cities of Berland. The cities of Berland have coordinates $$$10, 21, 32$$$, so to connect them you need two cables of length $$$11$$$ and $$$11$$$. The cities of Byteland have coordinates $$$14$$$ and $$$16$$$, so to connect them you need one cable of length $$$2$$$. Thus, the total length of all cables is $$$11 + 11 + 2 = 24$$$.

# 比兰特、伯兰特和有争议的城市

比兰特和伯兰特的城市位于数轴$$$Ox$$$上。此外，在这条数轴上还有有争议的城市，在各自看来它们都属于每个国家。因此，在直线$$$Ox$$$上有三种类型的城市：

- 比兰特的城市，

- 伯兰特的城市，

- 有争议的城市。

最近，项目BNET启动了——一个新一代的计算机网络。现在，两国的任务都是连接城市，使得该国的网络连通。

两国同意用BNET电缆连接城市对，方式如下：

- 如果只看比兰特的城市和有争议的城市，那么在得到的城市集合中，任何城市都应该能通过一条或多条电缆从任何其他城市到达，

- 如果只看伯兰特的城市和有争议的城市，那么在得到的城市集合中，任何城市都应该能通过一条或多条电缆从任何其他城市到达。

因此，有必要选择一组城市对用电缆连接，使得两个条件同时满足。电缆允许双向数据传输。每条电缆恰好连接两个不同的城市。

从一座城市到另一座城市铺设电缆的成本等于它们之间的距离。求铺设一组电缆的最小总成本，使得两个城市子集（比兰特和有争议的城市、伯兰特和有争议的城市）连通。

每座城市都是直线$$$Ox$$$上的一个点。从技术上讲，可以用电缆连接城市$$$a$$$和$$$b$$$，使得城市$$$c$$$（$$$a \lt c \lt b$$$）不连接到这条电缆，其中$$$a$$$、$$$b$$$和$$$c$$$同时是城市$$$a$$$、$$$b$$$和$$$c$$$的坐标。

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数$$$n$$$（$$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^{5}$$$）——城市的数量。

接下来的$$$n$$$行包含一个整数$$$x_i$$$和一个字母$$$c_i$$$（$$$-10^{9} \le x_i \le 10^{9}$$$）——城市的坐标及其类型。如果城市属于比兰特，$$$c_i$$$等于'`B`'。如果城市属于伯兰特，$$$c_i$$$等于«`R`»。如果有争议，$$$c_i$$$等于'`P`'。

所有城市的坐标互不相同。保证城市按其坐标递增的顺序给出。

## 输出

输出这样一组线缆的最小总长度：如果删除所有 Berland 城市（$$$c_i$$$='`R`'），仍然可以从任意剩余城市仅通过线缆到达任意其他剩余城市。类似地，如果删除所有 Byteland 城市（$$$c_i$$$='`B`'），仍然可以从任意剩余城市仅通过线缆到达任意其他剩余城市。

## 提示

在第一个示例中，你应该将第一座城市与第二座城市、第二座城市与第三座城市、第三座城市与第四座城市连接。线缆的总长度将为 $$$5 + 3 + 4 = 12$$$。

在第二个示例中没有争议城市，因此你需要连接 Byteland 的所有相邻城市以及 Berland 的所有相邻城市。Berland 的城市坐标为 $$$10, 21, 32$$$，因此要连接它们，你需要两条长度分别为 $$$11$$$ 和 $$$11$$$ 的线缆。Byteland 的城市坐标为 $$$14$$$ 和 $$$16$$$，因此要连接它们，你需要一条长度为 $$$2$$$ 的线缆。因此，所有线缆的总长度为 $$$11 + 11 + 2 = 24$$$。

# Minimal k-covering

You are given a bipartite graph *G* = (*U*, *V*, *E*), *U* is the set of vertices of the first part, *V* is the set of vertices of the second part and *E* is the set of edges. There might be multiple edges.

Let's call some subset of its edges ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e6fd4de7a5e51fb9e41d0da53a126fb1fa5b5816.png) *k*-covering iff the graph ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3d5f96647be417c8f189d1da2f2152840412ac15.png) has each of its vertices incident to at least *k* edges. Minimal *k*-covering is such a *k*-covering that the size of the subset ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e6fd4de7a5e51fb9e41d0da53a126fb1fa5b5816.png) is minimal possible.

Your task is to find minimal *k*-covering for each ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/36b710172cf0e7b4b9dc703e0dd4b4834e24f054.png), where *minDegree* is the minimal degree of any vertex in graph *G*.

## Input

The first line contains three integers *n*$_{1}$, *n*$_{2}$ and *m* (1 ≤ *n*$_{1}$, *n*$_{2}$ ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ *m* ≤ 2000) — the number of vertices in the first part, the number of vertices in the second part and the number of edges, respectively.

The *i*-th of the next *m* lines contain two integers *u*$_{i}$ and *v*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *u*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*$_{1}$, 1 ≤ *v*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*$_{2}$) — the description of the *i*-th edge, *u*$_{i}$ is the index of the vertex in the first part and *v*$_{i}$ is the index of the vertex in the second part.

## Output

For each ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/36b710172cf0e7b4b9dc703e0dd4b4834e24f054.png) print the subset of edges (minimal *k*-covering) in separate line.

The first integer *cnt*$_{k}$ of the *k*-th line is the number of edges in minimal *k*-covering of the graph. Then *cnt*$_{k}$ integers follow — original indices of the edges which belong to the minimal *k*-covering, these indices should be pairwise distinct. Edges are numbered 1 through *m* in order they are given in the input.
content.title: Minimal k-covering

# 最小 k-覆盖

给定一个二分图 *G* = (*U*, *V*, *E*)，*U* 是第一部分的顶点集合，*V* 是第二部分的顶点集合，*E* 是边的集合。可能存在多重边。

我们称其边的某个子集 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e6fd4de7a5e51fb9e41d0da53a126fb1fa5b5816.png) 为 *k*-覆盖，当且仅当图 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3d5f96647be417c8f189d1da2f2152840412ac15.png) 的每个顶点都至少关联 *k* 条边。最小 *k*-覆盖是指子集 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e6fd4de7a5e51fb9e41d0da53a126fb1fa5b5816.png) 的大小尽可能小的 *k*-覆盖。

你的任务是对每个 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/36b710172cf0e7b4b9dc703e0dd4b4834e24f054.png) 找到最小 *k*-覆盖，其中 *minDegree* 是图 *G* 中任意顶点的最小度数。

# Sand Fortress

You are going to the beach with the idea to build the greatest sand castle ever in your head! The beach is not as three-dimensional as you could have imagined, it can be decribed as a line of spots to pile up sand pillars. Spots are numbered 1 through infinity from left to right.

Obviously, there is not enough sand on the beach, so you brought *n* packs of sand with you. Let height *h*$_{i}$ of the sand pillar on some spot *i* be the number of sand packs you spent on it. You can't split a sand pack to multiple pillars, all the sand from it should go to a single one. There is a fence of height equal to the height of pillar with *H* sand packs to the left of the first spot and you should prevent sand from going over it.

Finally you ended up with the following conditions to building the castle:

- *h*$_{1}$ ≤ *H*: no sand from the leftmost spot should go over the fence;

- For any ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/759a40f66b7756c8c552aa9eba265b46676afca5.png) |*h*$_{i}$ - *h*$_{i + 1}$| ≤ 1: large difference in heights of two neighboring pillars can lead sand to fall down from the higher one to the lower, you really don't want this to happen;

- ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/72efe19561bd30eb9a2d4d6f86449bcbb93f464b.png): you want to spend all the sand you brought with you.

As you have infinite spots to build, it is always possible to come up with some valid castle structure. Though you want the castle to be as compact as possible.

Your task is to calculate the minimum number of spots you can occupy so that all the aforementioned conditions hold.

## Input

The only line contains two integer numbers *n* and *H* (1 ≤ *n*, *H* ≤ 10$^{18}$) — the number of sand packs you have and the height of the fence, respectively.

## Output

Print the minimum number of spots you can occupy so the all the castle building conditions hold.

## Note

Here are the heights of some valid castles:

- *n* = 5, *H* = 2, [2, 2, 1, 0, ...], [2, 1, 1, 1, 0, ...], [1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, ...]

- *n* = 6, *H* = 8, [3, 2, 1, 0, ...], [2, 2, 1, 1, 0, ...], [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 1, 0...] (this one has 5 spots occupied)

The first list for both cases is the optimal answer, 3 spots are occupied in them.

And here are some invalid ones:

- *n* = 5, *H* = 2, [3, 2, 0, ...], [2, 3, 0, ...], [1, 0, 2, 2, ...]

- *n* = 6, *H* = 8, [2, 2, 2, 0, ...], [6, 0, ...], [1, 4, 1, 0...], [2, 2, 1, 0, ...]

# Isomorphic Strings

You are given a string *s* of length *n* consisting of lowercase English letters.

For two given strings *s* and *t*, say *S* is the set of distinct characters of *s* and *T* is the set of distinct characters of *t*. The strings *s* and *t* are isomorphic if their lengths are equal and there is a one-to-one mapping (bijection) *f* between *S* and *T* for which *f*(*s*$_{i}$) = *t*$_{i}$. Formally:

- *f*(*s*$_{i}$) = *t*$_{i}$ for any index *i*,

- for any character ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/06141837c12bacfca2f66fcc1aca9166afa1a5ce.png) there is exactly one character ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8b0099ac39a2eb4880206793c01c80521177a489.png) that *f*(*x*) = *y*,

- for any character ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8b0099ac39a2eb4880206793c01c80521177a489.png) there is exactly one character ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/06141837c12bacfca2f66fcc1aca9166afa1a5ce.png) that *f*(*x*) = *y*.

For example, the strings "`aababc`" and "`bbcbcz`" are isomorphic. Also the strings "`aaaww`" and "`wwwaa`" are isomorphic. The following pairs of strings are not isomorphic: "`aab`" and "`bbb`", "`test`" and "`best`".

You have to handle *m* queries characterized by three integers *x*, *y*, *len* (1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n* - *len* + 1). For each query check if two substrings *s*[*x*... *x* + *len* - 1] and *s*[*y*... *y* + *len* - 1] are isomorphic.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated integers *n* and *m* (1 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$, 1 ≤ *m* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$) — the length of the string *s* and the number of queries.

The second line contains string *s* consisting of *n* lowercase English letters.

The following *m* lines contain a single query on each line: *x*$_{i}$, *y*$_{i}$ and *len*$_{i}$ (1 ≤ *x*$_{i}$, *y*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*, 1 ≤ *len*$_{i}$ ≤ *n* - *max*(*x*$_{i}$, *y*$_{i}$) + 1) — the description of the pair of the substrings to check.

## Output

For each query in a separate line print "`YES`" if substrings *s*[*x*$_{i}$... *x*$_{i}$ + *len*$_{i}$ - 1] and *s*[*y*$_{i}$... *y*$_{i}$ + *len*$_{i}$ - 1] are isomorphic and "`NO`" otherwise.

## Note

The queries in the example are following:

- substrings "`a`" and "`a`" are isomorphic: *f*(*a*) = *a*;

- substrings "`ab`" and "`ca`" are isomorphic: *f*(*a*) = *c*, *f*(*b*) = *a*;

- substrings "`bac`" and "`aba`" are not isomorphic since *f*(*b*) and *f*(*c*) must be equal to *a* at same time;

- substrings "`bac`" and "`cab`" are isomorphic: *f*(*b*) = *c*, *f*(*a*) = *a*, *f*(*c*) = *b*.

# 同构字符串

给定一个长度为 *n* 的字符串 *s*，由小写英文字母组成。

对于两个给定的字符串 *s* 和 *t*，设 *S* 为 *s* 的不同字符集合，*T* 为 *t* 的不同字符集合。如果两个字符串长度相等，且存在一个从 *S* 到 *T* 的一一映射（双射）*f*，使得对于任意下标 *i* 都有 *f*(*s*$_{i}$) = *t*$_{i}$，则称字符串 *s* 和 *t* 同构。形式化地说：

- 对于任意下标 *i*，*f*(*s*$_{i}$) = *t*$_{i}$，

- 对于任意字符 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/06141837c12bacfca2f66fcc1aca9166afa1a5ce.png)，恰好存在一个字符 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8b0099ac39a2eb4880206793c01c80521177a489.png) 使得 *f*(*x*) = *y*，

- 对于任意字符 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8b0099ac39a2eb4880206793c01c80521177a489.png)，恰好存在一个字符 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/06141837c12bacfca2f66fcc1aca9166afa1a5ce.png) 使得 *f*(*x*) = *y*。

例如，字符串 "`aababc`" 和 "`bbcbcz`" 是同构的。字符串 "`aaaww`" 和 "`wwwaa`" 也是同构的。以下字符串对不是同构的："`aab`" 和 "`bbb`"，"`test`" 和 "`best`"。

你需要处理 *m* 个查询，每个查询由三个整数 *x*、*y*、*len* 描述（1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n* - *len* + 1）。对于每个查询，检查两个子串 *s*[*x*... *x* + *len* - 1] 和 *s*[*y*... *y* + *len* - 1] 是否同构。

## 输入

第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 *n* 和 *m*（1 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$，1 ≤ *m* ≤ 2·10$^{5}$）——字符串 *s* 的长度和查询的数量。

第二行包含由 *n* 个小写英文字母组成的字符串 *s*。

接下来的 *m* 行每行包含一个查询：*x*$_{i}$、*y*$_{i}$ 和 *len*$_{i}$（1 ≤ *x*$_{i}$, *y*$_{i}$ ≤ *n*，1 ≤ *len*$_{i}$ ≤ *n* - *max*(*x*$_{i}$, *y*$_{i}$) + 1）——要检查的子串对的描述。

## 输出

对于每个查询，如果子串 *s*[*x*$_{i}$... *x*$_{i}$ + *len*$_{i}$ - 1] 和 *s*[*y*$_{i}$... *y*$_{i}$ + *len*$_{i}$ - 1] 同构，则在一行中输出 "`YES`"，否则输出 "`NO`"。

## 提示

示例中的查询如下：

- 子串 "`a`" 和 "`a`" 是同构的：*f*(*a*) = *a*；

- 子串 "`ab`" 和 "`ca`" 是同构的：*f*(*a*) = *c*，*f*(*b*) = *a*；

- 子串 "`bac`" 和 "`aba`" 不是同构的，因为 *f*(*b*) 和 *f*(*c*) 必须同时等于 *a*；

- 子串 "`bac`" 和 "`cab`" 是同构的：*f*(*b*) = *c*，*f*(*a*) = *a*，*f*(*c*) = *b*。

# Micro-World

You have a Petri dish with bacteria and you are preparing to dive into the harsh micro-world. But, unfortunately, you don't have any microscope nearby, so you can't watch them.

You know that you have $$$n$$$ bacteria in the Petri dish and size of the $$$i$$$-th bacteria is $$$a_i$$$. Also you know intergalactic positive integer constant $$$K$$$.

The $$$i$$$-th bacteria can swallow the $$$j$$$-th bacteria if and only if $$$a_i \gt a_j$$$ and $$$a_i \le a_j + K$$$. The $$$j$$$-th bacteria disappear, but the $$$i$$$-th bacteria doesn't change its size. The bacteria can perform multiple swallows. On each swallow operation any bacteria $$$i$$$ can swallow any bacteria $$$j$$$ if $$$a_i \gt a_j$$$ and $$$a_i \le a_j + K$$$. The swallow operations go one after another.

For example, the sequence of bacteria sizes $$$a=[101, 53, 42, 102, 101, 55, 54]$$$ and $$$K=1$$$. The one of possible sequences of swallows is: $$$[101, 53, 42, 102, \underline{101}, 55, 54]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[101, \underline{53}, 42, 102, 55, 54]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[\underline{101}, 42, 102, 55, 54]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[42, 102, 55, \underline{54}]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[42, 102, 55]$$$. In total there are $$$3$$$ bacteria remained in the Petri dish.

Since you don't have a microscope, you can only guess, what the minimal possible number of bacteria can remain in your Petri dish when you finally will find any microscope.

## Input

The first line contains two space separated positive integers $$$n$$$ and $$$K$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le K \le 10^6$$$) — number of bacteria and intergalactic constant $$$K$$$.

The second line contains $$$n$$$ space separated integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$) — sizes of bacteria you have.

## Output

Print the only integer — minimal possible number of bacteria can remain.

## Note

The first example is clarified in the problem statement.

In the second example an optimal possible sequence of swallows is: $$$[20, 15, 10, 15, \underline{20}, 25]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[20, 15, 10, \underline{15}, 25]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[20, 15, \underline{10}, 25]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[20, \underline{15}, 25]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[\underline{20}, 25]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[25]$$$.

In the third example no bacteria can swallow any other bacteria.

# 微观世界

你有一个培养皿，里面装有细菌，你正准备潜入这个严酷的微观世界。但不幸的是，你附近没有显微镜，所以无法观察它们。

你知道培养皿中有 $$$n$$$ 个细菌，第 $$$i$$$ 个细菌的大小为 $$$a_i$$$。你还知道一个星际正整数常数 $$$K$$$。

第$$$i$$$个细菌能够吞下第$$$j$$$个细菌，当且仅当$$$a_i \gt a_j$$$且$$$a_i \le a_j + K$$$。第$$$j$$$个细菌消失，但第$$$i$$$个细菌的大小不变。细菌可以进行多次吞食。在每次吞食操作中，任何细菌$$$i$$$都能吞下任何细菌$$$j$$$，如果$$$a_i \gt a_j$$$且$$$a_i \le a_j + K$$$。吞食操作依次进行。

例如，细菌大小序列为 $$$a=[101, 53, 42, 102, 101, 55, 54]$$$，且 $$$K=1$$$。一种可能的吞食序列是：$$$[101, 53, 42, 102, \underline{101}, 55, 54]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[101, \underline{53}, 42, 102, 55, 54]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[\underline{101}, 42, 102, 55, 54]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[42, 102, 55, \underline{54}]$$$ $$$\to$$$ $$$[42, 102, 55]$$$。最终培养皿中剩余了 $$$3$$$ 个细菌。

既然你没有显微镜，你只能猜测，当你最终找到任何显微镜时，你的培养皿中可能残留的细菌的最小可能数量是多少。

## 输入

第一行包含两个以空格分隔的正整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$K$$$（$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$，$$$1 \le K \le 10^6$$$）——细菌的数量和星际常数 $$$K$$$。

第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$（$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$）——你拥有的细菌大小。
